t: For financial assistance to eligible nonprofit organizations for housing for domestic farm labor, pursuant to section 516 of the Housing Act of 1949, as amended (42 U.S.C. 1486), $10,000,000, to remain available until expended.

fable.w: This is an appropriation of funds for financial assistance to nonprofit organizations for farm labor housing. The tempting reading is that mentioning nonprofit organizations brings outside parties into a federal decision, but they are only recipients of grant funding, and applications for benefits or grants are not participation. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue.
fable.s: For financial assistance to eligible nonprofit organizations for housing for domestic farm labor

opus.w: This provision only sets aside $10,000,000 for financial assistance to nonprofit organizations under section 516 of the Housing Act of 1949. Nonprofits are mentioned, but only as people who receive grants. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue. Receiving grants or benefits is specifically excluded from participation.
opus.s: For financial assistance to eligible nonprofit organizations for housing for domestic farm labor
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this counts as participation because it names "eligible nonprofit organizations," which are outside the federal government. That reading fails because the nonprofits only receive grant money. The definition specifically excludes applications for benefits or grants.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes appropriations for financial assistance (grants) to nonprofit organizations. The definition explicitly excludes 'applications for benefits or grants' from the scope of participation. There is no requirement for consultation, public comment, or advisory input from outside parties before the decision to appropriate funds is made.
qwen_chat.s: For financial assistance to eligible nonprofit organizations for housing for domestic farm labor, pursuant to section 516 of the Housing Act of 1949, as amended (42 U.S.C. 1486), $10,000,000, to remain available until expended.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the funds are for "eligible nonprofit organizations," there is an interaction between the government and outside entities. However, the definition explicitly states that "applications for benefits or grants" are not participation. This section is an appropriation for grants/financial assistance, not a requirement for consultation, public comment, or advisory input before a decision is made.
